subject: Science
lessonGoal: Students learn the core concepts of astronomy by exploring Earth, the Moon, the Solar System, gravity, stars, galaxies, and the tools scientists use to observe space.

sections.title: Introduction to Astronomy
sections.text: Welcome to Astronomy: Exploring Space. Astronomy is the study of everything beyond Earth, including the Moon, planets, stars, galaxies, and the universe itself. In this lesson, you will learn where Earth is in space, how the Solar System works, why the Moon changes shape, how seasons happen, how gravity creates orbits, what stars and galaxies are, and how telescopes help scientists observe objects that are extremely far away.

sections.title: Our Place in Space
sections.imageDescription: A clean beginner-friendly astronomy infographic on a #F7F8FB background. The image explains cosmic scale through three connected views: Earth inside the Solar System, the Solar System inside the Milky Way galaxy, and the Milky Way as one galaxy within the wider observable universe. The left view contains Earth, the Sun, and planets; the center view contains a spiral Milky Way with the Solar System marked; the right view contains many distant galaxies with the Milky Way highlighted. Soft colors, rounded labels, thin connector lines, gentle shadows, and light-to-medium text weight make the scale relationship easy for students to understand.

sections.title: Solar System Orbit Explorer
sections.htmlDescription: An interactive Solar System orbit explorer on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains how planets orbit the Sun and how planets differ in size, distance, and orbital speed. It contains a 2D top-down orbit layout, animated planet motion, clickable planets with simple fact cards, a distance comparison view, a pause/play control, an orbit speed slider, and a 3D GLB planet viewer. Each planet row has a View 3D chip that opens the selected planet model full-size on the left side, while the View orbit button returns to the current orbit animation. Soft planet colors, thin orbit rings, rounded cards, and light-to-medium typography give the activity a clean beginner-friendly style.

sections.title: The Sun, Earth, and Moon System
sections.imageDescription: A clear educational astronomy diagram on a #F7F8FB background showing the Sun, Earth, and Moon system. The image explains rotation, revolution, orbit, sunlight, and reflected moonlight. It contains the Sun sending light toward Earth, Earth rotating on its tilted axis, and the Moon orbiting Earth along a thin orbit path. Rounded labels identify the Sun, Earth, Moon, sunlight, reflected sunlight, Earth rotation, and Moon orbit. Soft yellow, blue, gray, and navy tones keep the diagram calm and readable.

sections.title: Moon Phase Simulator
sections.htmlDescription: An interactive Moon phase simulator on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains why the Moon appears to change shape from Earth even though half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. It contains Earth in the center, a movable Moon on a circular orbit, a fixed Sun direction marker, and a real-time Moon phase preview. As the Moon moves, the phase name and short explanation update for new moon, crescent, first quarter, gibbous, full moon, last quarter, and waning phases. Rounded controls and soft shadows make the simulator easy to use.

sections.title: Day, Night, and Seasons
sections.imageDescription: A beginner-friendly astronomy diagram on a #F7F8FB background explaining day, night, and seasons. The image contains a small Earth with one half lit and one half dark to show day and night from rotation. It also contains a four-position orbit diagram around the Sun showing spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Earth's axis stays tilted in the same direction in all four orbit positions. Simple arrows, soft sunlight rays, rounded labels, and light-to-medium typography separate Earth's daily rotation from its yearly revolution.

sections.title: Earth Tilt and Seasons Lab
sections.htmlDescription: An interactive Earth tilt and seasons lab on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains how Earth's tilted axis and yearly orbit cause seasons. It contains a position slider for Earth's place around the Sun, a tilt slider for axis angle, sunlight rays, Northern and Southern Hemisphere labels, and season labels for both hemispheres. The explanation card updates as Earth moves, showing which hemisphere receives more direct sunlight. Soft colors, thin orbital paths, and rounded control panels support a calm science-lab layout.

sections.title: Stars, Color, and Temperature
sections.imageDescription: A beginner-friendly star color and temperature chart on a #F7F8FB background. The image explains that star color gives clues about surface temperature. It contains a horizontal sequence from cooler red stars to hotter blue stars, including red, orange, yellow, white, and blue examples. The Sun appears as a yellow star example. A temperature arrow labeled cooler to hotter connects the star colors. Soft glow effects, rounded labels, and a short note about blue stars being hotter than red stars keep the chart simple and readable.

sections.title: Star Color Temperature Explorer
sections.htmlDescription: An interactive star color temperature explorer on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains the relationship between star temperature, color, and brightness. It contains a temperature slider, a large star preview that changes from red to orange to yellow to white to blue, an approximate temperature value, a color name, and an explanation card. A Sun marker sits near the yellow region for comparison. Rounded cards, soft glow effects, calm spacing, and light-to-medium typography make the explorer easy for beginners.

sections.title: The Life Cycle of Stars
sections.imageDescription: A star life cycle diagram on a #F7F8FB background. The image explains how stars are born, live, and end in different ways depending on their mass. It begins with a stellar nebula and branches into two paths. The average-star path includes main sequence star, red giant, planetary nebula, and white dwarf. The massive-star path includes massive main sequence star, red supergiant, supernova, and either neutron star or black hole. Flowing arrows, soft cosmic colors, rounded labels, and light-to-medium text weight make the branching sequence clear.

sections.title: Build a Star Life Cycle
sections.htmlDescription: A drag-and-drop star life cycle activity on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains how the stages of a star's life fit into either the average-star path or the massive-star path. It contains a nebula starting point, two branching lanes, draggable stage cards, rearrangeable drop areas, a check button, and gentle feedback for card placement. The activity supports experimentation before checking the answer. Rounded draggable cards, clear visual lanes, soft feedback states, and light-to-medium typography keep the activity simple and friendly.

sections.title: Galaxies and the Universe
sections.imageDescription: A clean astronomy diagram on a #F7F8FB background showing galaxy types and galaxy contents. The image explains that galaxies are huge collections of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter. It contains three labeled galaxy shapes: spiral, elliptical, and irregular. The Milky Way appears as a spiral galaxy example. Small callouts identify stars, gas clouds, dust lanes, and a dark matter halo. Soft blue, purple, gold, and gray tones, rounded labels, thin connector lines, and light-to-medium typography make the diagram easy to scan.

sections.title: Galaxy Sorter and Redshift Explorer
sections.htmlDescription: A combined galaxy sorting and redshift explorer on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains galaxy shapes and the idea that light from distant galaxies can shift toward red as space expands. It contains draggable galaxy cards sorted into spiral, elliptical, and irregular groups. It also contains a redshift slider that stretches a simple spectrum line to show wavelength increasing. A calm explanation panel connects redshift with distant galaxies moving away. Soft galaxy thumbnails, rounded drop zones, thin lines, and light-to-medium typography support a clean learning activity.

sections.title: How We Observe Space
sections.imageDescription: A diagram on a #F7F8FB background showing how scientists observe space with different tools and wavelengths of light. The image explains telescopes and observation methods. It contains an optical telescope observing visible light, a radio telescope receiving radio waves, a space telescope above Earth, and a spectroscopy strip that splits starlight into colors. Labels identify visible light, radio waves, space telescope, optical telescope, radio telescope, and spectrum. A clean layout, soft science colors, rounded labels, thin connector lines, and light-to-medium typography keep the observing tools organized.

sections.title: Astronomy Mission Planner
sections.htmlDescription: A final interactive astronomy mission planner on a #F7F8FB background. The interactive explains how different space questions need different observation tools. It contains target choices such as the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, a star, and a galaxy, along with tool choices such as an optical telescope, radio telescope, space telescope, rover, and flyby probe. The mission plan card summarizes the selected target, the chosen tool, the question being investigated, and the expected observation. Rounded option cards, soft icons, calm feedback, and light-to-medium typography make the planner feel like a beginner-friendly mission design activity.
